purpose: Candidate real-world gaming/game-engine repositories for BRE benchmark trials.
selection_criteria: Open-source GitHub repository verified with git ls-remote.
Gaming, game engine, game framework, physics, or game-server domain.
Primary language is Rust, TypeScript, or JavaScript so BRE can analyze imports today.

repos.why_benchmark: Large Rust ECS game engine with many crates, features, examples, and config surfaces.
repos.starter_task: Pick one focused example or subsystem and test whether BRE pulls the owning plugin/module plus Cargo feature context.

repos.why_benchmark: Production-sized 2D/3D Rust game engine with editor, demos, and workspace complexity.
repos.starter_task: Target a small demo or scene-loading path and measure whether BRE avoids dragging the whole engine into context.

repos.why_benchmark: Moderate-size Rust 2D framework; good for dependency and examples-to-core mapping.
repos.starter_task: Change an input/audio/windowing behavior and verify BRE selects the core module, example, Cargo.toml, and tests.

repos.why_benchmark: Rust cross-platform game library with examples and platform-specific code.
repos.starter_task: Target one example or input/rendering path and check whether BRE follows imports into the relevant platform/core files.

repos.why_benchmark: Bevy-focused physics engine with ECS components and plugin boundaries.
repos.starter_task: Change a collision or rigid-body behavior and check whether BRE selects component, plugin, and test/example context.

repos.why_benchmark: Rust bindings for Godot 4; good for FFI/bindings boundary context.
repos.starter_task: Target a binding API behavior and verify BRE selects generated/binding boundary context without loading generated bulk.

repos.why_benchmark: Minecraft server in Rust; real game-server domain with protocol, world, and config concerns.
repos.starter_task: Target a command/protocol handling path and measure whether BRE pulls protocol definitions and tests.

repos.why_benchmark: Rust Minecraft server framework; smaller than Pumpkin and good for protocol/context tests.
repos.starter_task: Change packet or entity behavior and check whether BRE selects protocol, entity, and example context.

repos.why_benchmark: Small Rust 2D game framework, suitable for fast trial loops.
repos.starter_task: Target a graphics/input module and verify BRE finds the core module plus example/test coverage.

repos.why_benchmark: Actual small Bevy game, not just an engine; good for gameplay-system context.
repos.starter_task: Change combat or map behavior and check whether BRE pulls the relevant Bevy systems/resources.

repos.why_benchmark: Actual Bevy side-scroller game with gameplay code and assets.
repos.starter_task: Target a player movement/combat issue and measure whether BRE selects systems, components, and config.

repos.why_benchmark: Large TypeScript 3D engine; useful stress test for context budgets and monorepo scale.
repos.starter_task: Target one package/subsystem and test whether BRE can avoid massive unrelated context.

repos.why_benchmark: Turn-based game state and multiplayer framework; good for reducer/state/test context.
repos.starter_task: Target move validation or multiplayer state sync and check whether BRE selects reducer, server, and test files.

repos.why_benchmark: 2D physics engine in TypeScript; useful for algorithmic code plus examples/tests.
repos.starter_task: Target collision/contact behavior and check whether BRE selects physics core and focused tests.

repos.why_benchmark: TypeScript 2D HTML5 game engine with real engine subsystems and docs/examples.
repos.starter_task: Target entity/input/collision behavior and measure whether BRE selects code, tests, and config.

repos.why_benchmark: JavaScript/TypeScript game library with examples and engine core.
repos.starter_task: Target sprite/input behavior and check whether BRE pulls the relevant source and examples.

repos.why_benchmark: Actual open-source 2D MMORPG, useful for client/server gameplay context.
repos.starter_task: Target inventory/combat/network flow and test whether BRE selects both client and server ownership files.

repos.why_benchmark: WebGL/WebGPU/WebXR runtime with engine subsystems and examples.
repos.starter_task: Target rendering/material/input behavior and verify BRE selects core engine files and tests.

repos.why_benchmark: Modern lightweight HTML5 game engine with JS/TS surface.
repos.starter_task: Target input, collision, or rendering behavior and measure context precision.

repos.why_benchmark: Small HTML5 game engine with low clone cost and fast smoke-test loops.
repos.starter_task: Target a compact engine behavior and check whether BRE can stay precise.
